key_insight: Gradient-flow theory can substantially overestimate plasticity recovery after pretraining because rare ReLU gate disagreements, not the average dynamics, control whether finite-batch SGD can separate the units.
engineering_relevance: For transfer, fine-tuning, and constitutive-model training, this means recovery may fail unless batch size and sample budget are large enough to resolve rare disagreement events, especially after long pretraining with weight decay.
method: Two-unit ReLU regression with a source task that aligns the neurons and a target task that rewards their separation.
Compare population gradient flow to online finite-batch SGD with step size η, batch size b, and weight decay λ across pretraining and target phases.
Track the exact online recursion and bound how often the model samples the narrow input wedge where the two gates disagree.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical recovery bounds plus simulations showing recovery depends mainly on the disagreement budget bδ/η and saturates with training horizon.
watch_item: The result is sharp for the analyzed two-unit ReLU setting, so extending the conclusion to deeper or non-ReLU models may require new disagreement-geometry estimates.
paper_title: Rare Gate Disagreements Can Limit Plasticity: When Gradient Flow Mispredicts Finite-Batch SGD
